questions.question: Explain why all four elements of the marketing mix must be consistent, using an example.
questions.correctAnswer: Consistency is essential because mixed signals confuse customers and damage the brand. Example: if a restaurant positions itself as fine dining (product: high-quality food), but charges fast-food prices (price), operates from a takeaway outlet (place), and advertises on budget billboards (promotion), customers won't know what to expect. The mix must align: fine dining = premium price, smart locati

questions.question: Describe how the marketing mix might differ for a budget airline compared to a luxury airline.
questions.correctAnswer: Budget airline: product = basic seat, no frills, charged for extras; price = low, competitive; place = online booking, secondary airports; promotion = price-led advertising, sales promotions, social media deals. Luxury airline: product = spacious seats, gourmet food, lounge access; price = premium; place = major airports, travel agents, direct booking; promotion = prestige advertising, partnership

questions.question: Evaluate whether a business should adapt its marketing mix when entering a foreign market.
questions.correctAnswer: Arguments for adaptation: different cultures have different preferences (McDonald's offers vegetarian-only outlets in India), local income levels require different pricing, distribution systems vary by country, and local media habits differ. questions.question: Full-Mark Response Evaluate the marketing mix of a new energy drink aimed at 16-24 year-old students, and suggest improvements. <div class="
questions.correctAnswer: A grade 9 response will: analyse the current mix (product: energy drink with caffeine and vitamins; price: competitive at £1.50; place: convenience stores and vending machines; promotion: social media ads); evaluate consistency (product and promotion align with youth market, but is the price right for students on budgets? Are convenience stores the best place when students spend time on campus?); suggest improvements: product (sugar-free version for health-conscious students), price (multi-pack discounts, student loyalty scheme), place (university campus vending, online subscription delivery), promotion (university ambassador programme, fresher's fair sampling, TikTok challenges); conclude: the basic mix is sound but needs refinement to truly penetrate the student market - campus-based distribution and student-specific promotions would significantly improve effectiveness.
